hints.title: Trip Sequence Chronology
hints.text: Assign sequential rank numbers to each driver trips sorted chronologically by trip date.

hints.title: Halfway Partitioning
hints.text: Partition each driver trips into the initial half and the subsequent half based on the median split.

hints.title: Efficiency Gain Filtering
hints.text: Compute the average distance per fuel unit for both halves and filter for drivers with positive improvement.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH ranked_trips AS (
    SELECT 
        trip_id,
        driver_id,
        trip_date,
        distance_km,
        fuel_liters,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY driver_id ORDER BY trip_date ASC, trip_id ASC) AS rn,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY driver_id) AS total_trips
    FROM trips
),
split_halves AS (
    SELECT 
        driver_id,
        AVG(CASE WHEN rn <= FLOOR(total_trips / 2.0) THEN (distance_km / fuel_liters) END) AS first_half_avg,
        AVG(CASE WHEN rn > CEIL(total_trips / 2.0) THEN (distance_km / fuel_liters) END) AS second_half_avg
    FROM ranked_trips
    WHERE total_trips >= 4
    GROUP BY driver_id
)
SELECT 
    d.driver_id,
    d.driver_name,
    ROUND(s.first_half_avg, 2) AS first_half_avg,
    ROUND(s.second_half_avg, 2) AS second_half_avg,
    ROUND(s.second_half_avg - s.first_half_avg, 2) AS efficiency_improvement
FROM split_halves s
JOIN drivers d ON s.driver_id = d.driver_id
WHERE s.second_half_avg > s.first_half_avg
ORDER BY efficiency_improvement DESC, d.driver_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Window ranking across driver trips followed by conditional aggregation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries per driver recalculate trip ranks repeatedly.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window functions compute counts and ranks in a single pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use window functions to partition trips chronologically and compare period averages.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def find_drivers_with_improved_fuel_efficiency(drivers: pd.DataFrame, trips: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    trips_sorted = trips.sort_values(by=['driver_id', 'trip_date', 'trip_id']).copy()
    trips_sorted['rn'] = trips_sorted.groupby('driver_id').cumcount() + 1
    trips_sorted['total_trips'] = trips_sorted.groupby('driver_id')['trip_id'].transform('count')
    
    # Filter drivers with at least 4 trips
    valid = trips_sorted[trips_sorted['total_trips'] >= 4].copy()
    valid['eff'] = valid['distance_km'] / valid['fuel_liters']
    
    first_half = valid[valid['rn'] <= np.floor(valid['total_trips'] / 2.0)]
    second_half = valid[valid['rn'] > np.ceil(valid['total_trips'] / 2.0)]
    
    f_avg = first_half.groupby('driver_id')['eff'].mean().reset_index(name='first_half_avg')
    s_avg = second_half.groupby('driver_id')['eff'].mean().reset_index(name='second_half_avg')
    
    merged = f_avg.merge(s_avg, on='driver_id', how='inner')
    merged = merged[merged['second_half_avg'] > merged['first_half_avg']].copy()
    merged['efficiency_improvement'] = (merged['second_half_avg'] - merged['first_half_avg']).round(2)
    merged['first_half_avg'] = merged['first_half_avg'].round(2)
    merged['second_half_avg'] = merged['second_half_avg'].round(2)
    
    res = merged.merge(drivers, on='driver_id', how='inner')
    res = res.sort_values(by=['efficiency_improvement', 'driver_id'], ascending=[False, True])
    return res[['driver_id', 'driver_name', 'first_half_avg', 'second_half_avg', 'efficiency_improvement']]
